title: Synergistic Activity of APOL3 and GBP1 in Antigen Cross-Presentation
content: Antigen cross-presentation by dendritic cells allows the induction of immune response (activation of cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells) against internalized components from pathogens or dying tumour cells, through export of these components from the lumen of phagosomes to the cell surface. Such export requires megapore formation in the phagosomal membrane, like also occurs in the outer membrane of mitochondria for cytochrome C export during apoptosis. Two interferon-induced proteins synergistically participate in this process: apolipoprotein L3 (APOL3) (or its murine homologue mAPOL7C), and the dynamin-like GTPase guanylate-binding protein 1 (GBP1). I propose that following membrane destabilization by GBP1, APOL3 can trigger pore formation through transmembrane insertion and cardiolipin solubilization. Moreover, both proteins could induce activation of non-muscular myosin 2A (NM2A) and pro-apoptotic BCL2-associated protein X (BAX), which allow phagosomal and mitochondrial pore expansion and stabilization into open megapores. Given the potential of its transmembrane a-helices for oligomerization, APOL3 may participate in inner coating of phagosomal membrane megapores.
